<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915585_theRebbe_828" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915585_theRebbe_828__p005">
  <section v="12">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the difference between the divine vitality that is felt within creations and the divine power of creation that is not felt, introducing the concept of "nature" as immersion.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">To say,</t>
    <t s="1">that the reason for this, that the concept of nature (from the term immersion) in the creation of creatures is brought in the discourses in a style of novelty</t>
    <t s="2">[that even in this one can say nature is from the term immersion30],</t>
    <t s="3">is because among the distinctions between the vitality of creatures and the creation of creatures is,</t>
    <t s="4">that the divine vitality that animates the creatures is revealed within the creatures,</t>
    <t s="5">so that it is felt in them that they have vitality,</t>
    <t s="6">and the matter of concealment is only that it is not felt that the vitality within them is divine vitality31,</t>
    <t s="7">but the creation of creatures</t>
    <t s="8">(that they were created from nothing to something)</t>
    <t s="9">is not felt within them.</t>
    <t s="10">For not only is it not felt in them that the creation is from G-dliness,</t>
    <t s="11">but the very matter of their creation is not felt within them32.</t>
    <t s="12">And the reason for this is,</t>
    <t s="13">because the divine vitality is invested within the creatures through concealing garments33.</t>
    <t s="14">[And since it is invested within the creatures, therefore it is felt in them,</t>
    <t s="15">except that due to the concealing garments it is not felt in them that it is divine vitality].</t>
    <t s="16">But the divine power that brings creatures into existence is separate from the creatures and is not invested within them33.</t>
    <t s="17">[And therefore their creation is not felt within the creatures].</t>
  </section>
  <section v="13">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section clarifies that "nature" as immersion primarily applies to the vitality invested in creatures, while the concealment of the creative power is due to its separateness.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And based on this, we can explain,</t>
    <t s="1">that the concept of nature (from the term immersion) is primarily in the vitality of creatures,</t>
    <t s="2">for the matter of immersion is that the immersed object is within the water and thereby the water covers it,</t>
    <t s="3">for in the analogy,</t>
    <t s="4">the divine vitality is invested within the creatures and thereby they conceal it.</t>
    <t s="5">But not so the concealment in the matter of creation, which is because the divine power that brings creatures into existence is separate from them and is not invested within them.</t>
    <t s="6">And the concept of nature (from the term immersion) regarding the power that brings into existence is</t>
    <t s="7">(primarily)</t>
    <t s="8">in the matter of concealment</t>
    <t s="9">(and not in the manner of concealment)34.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="14">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section discusses the two types of form—the true form (the soul) and the form of matter—and applies this to nature as the divine vitality of the world and the form of creatures.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">7)</t>
    <t s="1">And behold, it is explained elsewhere35,</t>
    <t s="2">that there are two matters of form.</t>
    <t s="3">The true form,</t>
    <t s="4">which is the soul,</t>
    <t s="5">and the matter of the body,</t>
    <t s="6">which is also called by the name "form,"</t>
    <t s="7">the form of matter.</t>
    <t s="8">And these two matters are related to each other,</t>
    <t s="9">for the form of the body is a vessel for the soul.</t>
    <t s="10">And based on this,</t>
    <t s="11">even though the primary matter of the seal of Adam HaRishon</t>
    <t s="12">(the form of the human species)</t>
    <t s="13">is the soul-form</t>
    <t s="14">(as explained above in section 5 of the discourses),</t>
    <t s="15">this also applies to the form of the human body36.</t>
    <t s="16">And from this it is also understood regarding nature,</t>
    <t s="17">that the primary matter of nature</t>
    <t s="18">(according to the interpretation that nature is from the term "the Holy One, blessed be He, imprinted every person with the seal of Adam HaRishon")</t>
    <t s="19">is the divine vitality of the world, which is the soul of the world,</t>
    <t s="20">and this also applies to the form of creatures,</t>
    <t s="21">the form of matter.</t>
    <t s="22">For the form of creatures is the vessel for the vitality and soul within them.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
